themes.name: Returns slower or lower than expected
themes.definition: User expected visible growth soon after starting and is disappointed by small, flat or negative returns in the first months.

themes.name: Anxiety from seeing losses
themes.definition: Seeing red numbers, a falling portfolio value or "-x%" causes worry, regret or the urge to stop or withdraw.

themes.name: Confusion about how returns are shown
themes.definition: Confused by NAV, units, absolute vs XIRR/annualised returns, current vs invested value, or why numbers don't add up.

themes.name: No sense of progress or reason to stay
themes.definition: Investing feels invisible or boring; no milestones, no link to a goal, user forgets why they started or stops engaging.

themes.name: Market news and crash headlines
themes.definition: News, social media or market falls create doubt about whether to keep investing.

themes.name: Started without a personal goal
themes.definition: SIP was started without a specific goal, amount logic or time horizon ("just to start investing").

themes.name: Started because of an influencer or peer
themes.definition: Started because of a YouTuber, finfluencer, friend, colleague or family member rather than their own plan.

themes.name: Doubt about having picked the wrong fund
themes.definition: Wonders if their fund is bad, compares with other funds, wants to switch or stops to "pick a better one".

themes.name: Moving money to something that looks better
themes.definition: Stops or reduces SIP to put money into stocks, F&O, crypto, gold, FD, real estate or another product, or diverts it to spending (bike, holiday, gifts - "lifestyle drift").

themes.name: Can't afford the instalment right now
themes.definition: Expenses, EMIs, job loss, emergency, irregular income or a big purchase make the monthly amount hard to keep paying.

themes.name: Debit date doesn't match when money arrives
themes.definition: SIP date falls before salary/income arrives, causing insufficient-balance failures or stress around the debit date.

themes.name: Autopay / mandate / payment problems
themes.definition: Mandate setup, approval, expiry or cancellation, UPI autopay, bank account closed or blocked, failed or missed debits, bounce charges, instalments not processed, or SIP auto-cancelled after repeated bounces.

themes.name: Can't flex the SIP (pause, skip, amount, date, frequency)
themes.definition: Wants to pause, skip, lower, raise, step up, or change the date or frequency of a SIP and can't, doesn't know how, or the option is limited or broken; a paused SIP was forgotten or never resumed. (If a change actually broke or cancelled the SIP, use modification_cancels_sip.)

themes.name: Changing the SIP breaks or cancels it
themes.definition: A step-up, amount or date change (or similar edit) led to the SIP being cancelled, duplicated, shown with the wrong amount, or a confusing 'SIP cancelled' message, without the user meaning to stop. Also cancel-and-recreate being the only way to change a SIP.

themes.name: Change in investor details breaks the SIP
themes.definition: A change in the investor's own status or details - NRI status, city or address, KYC, nominee, bank account details - causes the SIP to be cancelled or stuck.

themes.name: SIP ended when its fixed tenure ran out
themes.definition: The SIP stopped because its end date or number of instalments was reached, not because the user decided to stop.

themes.name: Withdrew money for a need
themes.definition: Redeemed or wanted to redeem SIP money for a need, often followed by stopping the SIP.

themes.name: Confusion about tax, exit load or charges
themes.definition: Unclear about capital gains tax, exit load, lock-in, stamp duty or hidden charges.

themes.name: App glitches or trust concerns
themes.definition: Bugs, wrong values, delays in units/NAV allotment, units or SIPs missing from the dashboard, app status that disagrees with the AMC/registrar, login issues, or worries about whether money is safe ('scam').

themes.name: Couldn't get help when stuck
themes.definition: Couldn't reach support or got no clear answer for a SIP problem.

themes.name: Moving SIPs to another platform
themes.definition: Stops SIPs on this app to continue them elsewhere (MF Central, AMC website, another app), or plans to.

themes.name: Too many funds or choices
themes.definition: Feels overwhelmed managing several SIPs/funds or too much information in the app.

themes.name: Set-and-forget automation keeps them going
themes.definition: User continues because the SIP is automatic and they don't have to think about it.

themes.name: Understanding of long-term investing / averaging
themes.definition: User continues because they understand compounding, rupee-cost averaging, or that early volatility is normal.

themes.name: SIP tied to a clear goal
themes.definition: User continues because the SIP is linked to a concrete goal (emergency fund, house, wedding, retirement).

themes.name: Reassured by a trusted person or community
themes.definition: Someone (friend, forum, advisor, video) reassured them to keep going during doubt.

themes.name: Fund stopped accepting SIPs
themes.definition: The AMC or fund stopped or restricted new SIPs or lump sums (e.g. international fund limits, small-cap inflow caps), so the investor's SIP was paused, cancelled or converted without their choice.

themes.name: Misunderstands how a SIP works
themes.definition: Misconceptions or basic confusion about SIP mechanics - fixed 'SIP tenure' (e.g. a '1-year SIP'), monthly interest, refunds on cancelling, needing to withdraw when the SIP 'ends', units/NAV, how to start, stop or withdraw, SIP vs insurance (ULIP) - that can lead to wrong decisions.

themes.name: Starting out (no problem stated)
themes.definition: Describes having just started or planning to start a SIP, with no problem or worry stated. Use only when nothing else fits.

themes.name: Other
themes.definition: Relevant to SIP continuation but none of the above fits. Describe it in other_theme_note.

rules: A market fall is a TRIGGER, not a theme. Code the reason the fall led to stopping: what they expected (expectation_mismatch), what they saw (red_number_anxiety), or what they misunderstood (return_metric_confusion). Use market_news_noise only when news or headlines themselves are the stated driver.
If an instalment failed and the user did not choose to stop, drop_mechanism is passive_lapse, even if they later gave up.
If they paused and the text says they never restarted or forgot, drop_mechanism is pause_not_resumed.
A complaint about the app with no link to SIP behaviour (e.g. a login bug while trading stocks) is not relevant.
Advice given TO others (common on Reddit, e.g. 'never stop your SIP') is relevant only if it describes the writer's own or someone's real experience; otherwise mark relevant=false.
first_time_investor = yes only if the text says so ('my first SIP', 'new to investing', 'started 3 months ago'). Use likely for strong hints, otherwise unclear.
When several themes are present, primary_theme is the one closest to the decision to stop, pause or continue.

Record only what the author says they did, checked, considered or changed. Keep observed behaviour separate from your interpretation; if a label rests on interpretation, evidence_strength is indirect_clue.
evidence_strength: direct_statement = the label is explicit in the comment; indirect_clue = the interpretation is supported but not stated; unclear = not enough evidence.

sip_action = struggling when the author is still investing but finding it hard (money, doubt, payment trouble) and has NOT said they are thinking of pausing or stopping. Once they mention pausing, reducing or stopping, use considering_stop.
Use the 'unclear' / 'none_mentioned' options whenever the comment does not give enough evidence. Never fill a field from what is typical.

If the SIP was cancelled, duplicated or broken by the platform, AMC or registrar after an action the user did NOT intend as stopping (step-up, amount or date change, moving platform, change of city, NRI or KYC status), drop_mechanism = system_cancelled. Theme = modification_cancels_sip for SIP changes, account_status_change for changes to the investor's own details.

If an AMC/registrar message and the app disagree (e.g. AMC says cancelled, app says active; units allotted but not shown), the theme is app_trust_reliability unless the mismatch followed a SIP change, in which case modification_cancels_sip.
If the user blames a specific fund ('this fund is not giving returns'), use fund_choice_doubt. If they blame the timeline or what they expected investing to do, use expectation_mismatch.
Stopping SIPs on this app to continue them elsewhere is platform_switch, not a stop of investing - but it still counts as a drop for this app.
A poll or question to the community with no personal situation ('Are you all continuing or pausing?') is relevant=false. If the author describes their own situation, it is relevant.
Many Reddit items are post titles only. Label only what the given text says; do not use knowledge of the full post.

trigger is the EVENT just before the change in behaviour (market fall, failed debit, expense shock, seeing returns, news, a SIP change, someone's advice). primary_theme is WHY that event led to the change. They are coded separately so 'the market fell' never stands in for the cause.
app_area is the part of the app the problem happens in or is noticed in. Use none_mentioned if the text doesn't point to one.
start_reason and money_source only when the text says so (e.g. 'started for tax saving', 'from my first salary', 'my dad gives me pocket money').
